lesson.title: Understanding a Quarter

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: A quarter means four equal parts that make up a whole group together (Source: Section 1). This means if you divide something into four pieces, each piece must be the same size.

sections.title: Example of a Quarter
sections.content: To see how this works with numbers, look at twelve counters. A quarter of twelve counters is three counters (Source: Section 1).

lesson.summary: A quarter represents one of four equal parts in a group. For example, if you have twelve items, one quarter is three items.

lesson.title: Understanding One Quarter

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: One quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole (Source: Section 1). This means if you take a whole object and divide it into four pieces that are all the same size, each piece is called one quarter.

sections.title: Example with Counters
sections.content: To see how this works with numbers, look at twelve counters. If you divide twelve counters into four equal parts, one quarter of those counters is three counters (Source: Section 1).

lesson.title: Cup Observations

sections.title: Volume at Noon and One O'clock
sections.content: The source provides two specific observations about the amount of liquid in a cup. At noon, the cup held 70 mL. By one o'clock, after 20 mL was added, the cup held 90 mL.

sections.title: Explanation of Observations
sections.content:
The two observations show how the volume changed over time:

1. The first observation is the starting amount: 70 mL at noon.
2. The second observation shows the final amount: 90 mL at one o'clock.

The difference between these two times is 20 mL, which was added to the cup.

lesson.summary: The observations show that a cup started with 70 mL of liquid at noon and increased to 90 mL by one o'clock after 20 mL was added.

lesson.title: Understanding Halves

sections.title: What is a Half?
sections.content: A half is one of two equal groups. When you put these two equal groups together, they make the whole collection (Source: Section 1).

sections.title: Finding a Half
sections.content: To find a half, you split a group into two parts that are the same size. For example, if a jar holds eight seeds, a half is four seeds (Source: Section 1).

lesson.summary: A half is one of two equal groups that make up a whole. In a group of eight seeds, four seeds make one half.
objectives: Explain a half using simple words
